levels.title: First to Arrive
levels.description: Two cars at a four-way stop. Who goes first?

stepRules.car-1: Arrived at the stop first, so it proceeds first.
stepRules.car-2: Arrived second — waits until the first car clears the intersection.

collisionRules.car-2>car-1: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives and stops first has the right of way. Car 2 arrived second and must wait.
collisionRules.*: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive and stop goes first.

levels.title: Arrived Together
levels.description: Two cars reach the stop at the same moment. Yield to the right.

stepRules.car-2: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one with no vehicle on its right goes first. Nothing is to Car 2's right.
stepRules.car-1: Car 2 is on Car 1's right, so Car 1 yields and goes second.

collisionRules.car-1>car-2: When vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right of way. Car 2 is to Car 1's right.
collisionRules.*: When you arrive at the same time as another vehicle, yield to the one on your right.

levels.title: Pedestrian Crossing
levels.description: A pedestrian is in the crosswalk as a car approaches.

stepRules.ped-1: Pedestrians in a crosswalk always have the right of way.
stepRules.car-1: Must wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing before proceeding.

collisionRules.car-1>ped-1: Pedestrians in a crosswalk have the right of way. You must always yield to them before proceeding.
collisionRules.*: Always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.

levels.title: Three at the Stop
levels.description: Three cars at a four-way stop. Combine arrival order and yielding right.

stepRules.car-2: Of the two cars that arrived next, nothing is to Car 2's right, so it goes before Car 3.
stepRules.car-3: Car 2 is on Car 3's right, so Car 3 goes last.

collisionRules.car-2>car-1: Car 1 arrived first and has priority over everyone.
collisionRules.car-3>car-1: Car 1 arrived first and has priority over everyone.
collisionRules.car-3>car-2: Car 2 and Car 3 arrived together — Car 2 has no one on its right, so it goes before Car 3.
collisionRules.*: First to arrive goes first; when two tie, yield to the one on the right.

levels.title: Turning Left
levels.description: A car turning left faces oncoming traffic on a green light.

stepRules.car-2: Going straight on a green light — has the right of way over oncoming left-turning traffic.
stepRules.car-1: Turning left must yield to oncoming traffic going straight, even on a green light.

collisionRules.car-1>car-2: A left-turning vehicle must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right.
collisionRules.*: Left turns yield to oncoming straight traffic.

levels.title: T-Intersection
levels.description: A car enters from a side road onto a through road.

stepRules.car-2: Traveling on the through road — has the right of way.
stepRules.car-1: Entering from the terminating side road must yield to all traffic on the through road.

collisionRules.car-1>car-2: A driver entering a through road from a terminating road at a T-intersection must yield to traffic already on the through road.
collisionRules.*: Yield to traffic already on the through road.

levels.title: No Signs At All
levels.description: An uncontrolled intersection with no signs or signals.

stepRules.car-1: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right. Nothing is to Car 1's right, so it goes first.
stepRules.car-2: Car 1 is on Car 2's right, so Car 2 yields.

collisionRules.car-2>car-1: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield to vehicles approaching from your right. Car 1 is on Car 2's right.
collisionRules.*: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

levels.title: Sharing With a Cyclist
levels.description: A bicycle and a car at a four-way stop.

stepRules.cyclist-1: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. This cyclist arrived first, so it goes first.
stepRules.car-1: Must treat the bicycle like any other vehicle and wait its turn.

collisionRules.car-1>cyclist-1: Bicycles are treated as vehicles at intersections. The cyclist arrived first and has the right of way.
collisionRules.*: Treat bicycles as vehicles — the one that arrived first goes first.

levels.title: Reading the Signals
levels.description: A green left arrow for one car, a red light for the other.

stepRules.car-1: A green left-turn arrow gives a protected left turn — proceed.
stepRules.car-2: Facing a red light — must stop and wait for a green signal.

collisionRules.car-2>car-1: A red light means stop. Car 1 has a green arrow and the protected right of way.
collisionRules.*: Obey the signal — green proceeds, red stops.

levels.title: Emergency Vehicle
levels.description: An ambulance with lights and siren is approaching the stop.

stepRules.emergency-1: An emergency vehicle with siren and lights on has the right of way over everyone — let it pass first.
stepRules.car-1: After the emergency vehicle clears, normal rules resume — Car 1 arrived first.

collisionRules.car-1>emergency-1: You must always yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and lights, even if you have the right of way.
collisionRules.car-2>emergency-1: You must always yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and lights, even if you have the right of way.
collisionRules.car-2>car-1: After the emergency vehicle passes, Car 1 still has priority — it arrived first.
collisionRules.*: Yield to emergency vehicles first, then follow normal right-of-way.
